children: will shorten its name to Novo as the Danish drugmaker seeks to strengthen its brand as it battles Eli Lilly
for dominance in the obesity-drug market.

The company will also update its logo, with its trademark bull shifting to face right, Novo said Monday. The changes come as Lilly increasingly adopts a single-name identity, dropping “Eli” from its marketing materials.
At its Capital Markets Day on September 21 in London, Novo will provide a detailed overview of the updated corporate strategy.
CEO Mike Doustdar is pushing to make Novo leaner and more competitive as the company works to regain market share in obesity treatments.

“People have always been at the centre of Novo’s science. We have transformed major areas of healthcare, such as obesity and diabetes, by bringing innovation to conditions that affect millions of lives. But the unmet need remains vast, and at the same time, people's expectations of healthcare are changing,” said Doustdar. “Healthcare must become more responsive, relevant and easier to fit into everyday life. Our brand and culture are strategically important and will enhance how we operate and compete, but the reason we exist will not change. We remain true to our purpose of changing people’s lives and are ambitious about our future to help them have lasting health, starting right now."

Dropping “Nordisk” also removes a link to the company’s history. Novo Nordisk was formed in 1989 through the merger of Nordisk Insulinlaboratorium, founded in 1923, and Novo, established by former Nordisk employees two years later.

title: Novo Nordisk rebrands as ‘Novo’ in push to win back obesity market
